change.title: ao-replay/8764-r2
change.description:
fix(mobile): never restore a page over one the user moved to
fix(mobile): hold the update screen during onboarding and pairing
fix(mobile): keep root-level sheets out of the page restored after an update
fix(mobile): compare whole routes when restoring; hide the update screen's hidden half from VoiceOver
change.author: Prasad-D-Ware

findings.title: isSetupRoute misses /connect, the manual-pairing page
findings.body: The doc comment and PR intent say the update screen must wait during "onboarding and pairing". `app/_layout.tsx:267-270` describes pairing as two pages: the scanner (`/pair`) and the manual form pushed over it (`/connect`). `sheetResult.ts:73` pushes `/connect`. `isSetupRoute` only matches `/onboarding` and `/pair`, so an update that lands (or a foreground prompt) while the user fills in the manual connect form still raises the update screen over it. A Restart there throws away the half-typed host and credentials. `updateResume.ts` already treats `/connect` as setup (in `TRANSIENT`), so the two lists disagree. Add `connect` to the regex and to the test in `updates.test.ts`.

findings.title: New restore-timing logic has no test
findings.body: The behavior that changed most is in this hook: the restore no longer waits for `config`, `landing` is captured on the first ready render, and a later route change drops the restore. Only the pure `restoreAction` is tested. The scenario where `saved` resolves after the user has already navigated away (expected: no navigation) is not covered. A hook test would pin it. This also depends on `usePathname` already reporting the real landing route when `navState.key` first appears. If it first reports `/` and then the deep link, the restore is silently dropped. I could not confirm that ordering from the repo code.

contracts.action: Restore the saved page after an OTA restart without waiting for the store's config
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous version of the same effect, gated on `config !== null`. A cold-start notification tap also opens a page before the machine has answered.
contracts.before_after: Before: waited for config, then compared only path with saved path. After: runs once navigation has a key and storage is read, compares full hrefs against the landing route captured at first ready render, and drops the restore if the user has moved. `restored` is set before acting, so it fires once.
contracts.visible_effect: Reopens the saved page (push over the board, or replace a stale deep-linked page) as soon as navigation is ready. If the user has already moved, nothing happens.
contracts.failure_mode: If `takeResumeRoute` rejects, `saved` stays undefined and nothing is restored, with no error shown (the user just lands on the board). The effect never sets `restored`, but there is no retry either. Whether `usePathname` is final when `navState.key` first appears is not confirmed.

contracts.action: Hold the update screen while on onboarding or pairing, and offer it when the user leaves
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous effect offered as soon as an update was pending. The foreground 'prompt' path now has the same guard.
contracts.before_after: Before: offered regardless of route. After: `shouldOfferUpdate` also checks `pathname`, and the effect depends on `pathname`, so leaving a setup route re-runs it. `lastOffered` is only set when the screen is actually shown. The foreground prompt skips on a setup route but does not re-offer afterwards.
contracts.visible_effect: The update screen appears only outside onboarding and `/pair`. It still appears over `/connect`, the manual-pairing page.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent miss: an update that was already offered and put off, then prompted on foreground during a setup route, is not re-offered after leaving. This is acceptable because the next long absence offers it again. `/connect` is not covered (see finding).

summary: Small, coherent change. One real gap: `isSetupRoute` doesn't cover `/connect`, the manual-pairing page, so the update screen can still appear over it even though the intent is to hold it back during pairing. The new restore-timing logic in `UpdateRouteKeeper` is covered only through the pure `restoreAction` tests, which I raised as a low-confidence test gap. The a11y changes and the transient-route list match the layout's sheet declarations.
